messages:
mina: follow-up from today's allocator sync: proposing a two-pronged approach to cut fragmentation from tiny async offloads — a coalescing free-list + micro-allocator for hot tiny-objects.

chao: tl;dr?

mina: 1) defer small frees into a per-arena short-term ring (free-queue) that tries to coalesce adjacent tiny frees into a larger freeblock before returning to the global free list; 2) add a tiny-object suballocator (micro-allocator) that carves 64KB superblocks and packs many tiny keys to avoid scattering.

rishi: that sounds like a classic compact-on-free + pooling idea. what's the cost model? extra CPU on free, plus bookkeeping for superblocks.

mina: yep. expected tradeoffs: slightly more CPU at free-time (coalesce attempts limited, heuristics) vs fewer compaction cycles and better slab locality. Micro-allocator reduces metadata overhead per-key.

chao: how do we decide adjacency for coalesce? we don't have full virtual adjacency info for everything after async evict.

mina: we maintain physical page-aligned tags for tiny allocations so the free-queue stores (arena_id,page_off,size). Coalesce only within same page-range or adjacent pages. No global scan. cheap O(1) checks when inserting to ring.

rishi: race conditions? concurrent frees + allocs might miss coalesces or double-claim. need lock-free-ish or fine-grained per-page locks.

mina: plan: per-page spin-lock in the hotpath. cheap under normal load; fallback to try-lock and push to slow-path background coalescer if lock contended. The background coalescer periodically scans free-queue and merges entries.

ops-bot: note: background coalescer should be backpressure-aware to avoid stealing CPU during peak inference.

mina: agreed. coalescer runs with IO priority and a budget of CPU-ms/second per-node. Also we expose a console knob to throttle it.

chao: micro-allocator details? fragmentation internal vs external?

mina: micro-allocator allocates 64KB superblocks aligned to 64KB. Each superblock has a tiny bitmap and freelist; we pack keys by size-class (e.g., 32B,128B,512B). Freeing within superblock goes to that superblock's freelist. When superblock is sparse beyond threshold, we evacuate live items (background) and return whole superblock to global pool. That makes compaction cheaper (we move fewer live objects).

rishi: evacuation copies sound expensive. need to ensure it's background and rate-limited. Also eviction interplay: if tenant eviction wants to reclaim specific keys, do we support partial free without evacuate?

mina: yes: eviction can free individual slots immediately (they go to superblock freelist). Only when sparse ratio hits threshold do we schedule evacuation to consolidate. Evacuation uses sampled IO budget and piggybacks on normal compactor windows.

ops-bot: telemetry checklist added: superblock occupancy histogram, coalesce success rate, background evac bytes/sec, avg free-time latency, and per-tenant superblock counts.

chao: what about multi-tenant fairness and DoS? a tenant could allocate lots of tiny keys to hoard superblocks.

mina: we enforce per-tenant superblock quotas and an LRU reclaim order across tenants. Tenants exceeding quota get allocation failure or forced reclamation of their least-recently-used superblocks. We'll surface quota in Console and emit allocation rejection events.

rishi: can we simulate worst-case? want a bench: 1M tiny allocations churn with mixed long-lived small pins.

bench-bot: queued: `microalloc_bench --id=mb_9888 --allocs=1e6 --sizes=32,128,512 --pin_rate=0.1 --runs=5` on benchpool-2.

mina: initial microbench (prototype) results: occupancy up ~22% (more packed), compaction cycles down ~30%, p95 latency improved 8ms in steady chat mix; free CPU up ~5% and occasional p99 free latency spikes when background evac kicks in. Need to tune evac windows.

chao: good start. include adaptive evac thresholds: raise threshold under CPU pressure, lower threshold when compaction rate grows. Also jitter evac timing to avoid synchronized scans.

rishi: one more: make superblock layout friendly to GPU memcpy when moving blocks between host staging and device. Align to 4K/64K to allow efficient DMA.

mina: yes, align superblocks to GPU page boundaries and use batched memcpy for evacuation to minimize PCIe overhead.

ops-bot: implementation plan accepted for alpha: runtime-local only, coalescer + microalloc flags off by default.

mina: next steps: add design note to arch repo, wire minimal telemetry, land microalloc prototype behind runtime flag, run bench suite and attacker-style malicious tenant test, then iterate thresholds. I'll post results in 72h.

chao: thanks. ping infra for CPU budget knob.

rishi: volunteer to help on memcpy batching changes.

ops-bot: scheduled job: `microalloc_bench --ref=mb_9888 --notify=#eng-runtime`
